## Exp 1 — label / output-format interventions (768 logic examples = Items+Families+Nonwords; first-character accuracy)

`acc` = semantic accuracy (answer maps to the instruction's own label for the true verdict). `P(valid)` = fraction of responses giving the *valid* verdict (semantic), `P(lit1st)` = fraction producing the label listed first in the instruction (literal). `invalid` = response outside the two labels. `AUC` = threshold-free discrimination of the valid-vs-invalid logit margin; `thr-acc` = accuracy of the best single margin threshold.

## Exp 3 — counterfactual patching of MVS coordinates

448 matched pairs (same rule/antecedent/consequent sentences and marker; fact↔conclusion roles swapped: MP↔AC, MT↔DA, ± negated consequent), mean 7.0 differing token positions of equal-length prompts; test contents only. Each pair is used in both directions (896 trials). `transfer` = mean shift of the semantic margin toward the source ÷ mean source−target gap (1 = full transplant, 0 = nothing); `flip` = fraction of clean trials (target and source both answered correctly) whose verdict becomes the source's.
